Once again, something appears to be happening behind the scenes.

President Trump just explicitly called on Nvidia's, $NVDA, board to rehire Jensen Huang.

On top of this, he said Jensen returning would be "the best thing for the USA."

Just 10 days ago, Trump was calling for Tim Cook to replace Jensen Huang.

Hours ago, Treasury Secretary Bessent reversed his previous demand that Nvidia hire an "outside CEO." 

When asked whether Jensen Huang could return, Bessent responded, "Jensen is on the outside now," acknowledging that he could return.

Attorney General Todd Blanche has also questioned the allegations surrounding Huang's departure, saying he has "certainly" not concluded that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy.

In a matter of days, the Trump Admin's public position has shifted from calling for Jensen Huang's replacement to openly supporting his reinstatement.

The Trump Administration and Nvidia's shareholders appear to be aligned.

Pressure on Nvidia's board is mounting.

US businesses are forming at an unprecedented rate:

There were 501,609 US new business applications in October.

This marks the 7th consecutive month with business formation above 500,000.

This is also more than double the 235,730 recorded in April 2020, during the pandemic.

Since January 2025, new business applications have averaged 495,666 per month.

By comparison, the 2018-2019 pre-pandemic average stood at 292,344, or 41% lower.

The rapid adoption of AI is making it easier and cheaper to launch new businesses.

US entrepreneurial activity is skyrocketing.

The bears are having their moment.

After predicting a top in the AI trade every month for the last 4 years, the bears finally got their moment last week.

However, in 3 to 6 months, we are going to look back at this correction and realize it was just that: a correction.

There is a widespread narrative right now that Nvidia, $NVDA, is quite literally going to collapse. This is a stock that was trading at a record high on October 6th, worth nearly $6 trillion, and the inventor of the most advanced chips in the world (it's not even close).

That's how deeply pessimistic sentiment has become over the last seven weeks.

Even if Nvidia produced half as much revenue as they are guiding for their next fiscal year, this company would still produce close to $400 billion in annual revenue.

Meanwhile, the S&P 500 has posted three consecutive quarters with earnings growth above 25% and eight straight quarters of double-digit growth.

And, sentiment flipped so quickly that the S&P 500 closed the week 4.1 standard deviations below its 50-day moving average on Friday. Not even 2020 and 2008 saw such an occurrence.

The reality is that AI truly is the "next big thing" and the AI buildout is only accelerating.

Bears will sound smart, bulls will make money.

BREAKING: The median US home-sale price fell -0.4% YoY in October, to $388,634, posting its first YoY decline since May 2023.

This marks a sharp reversal from the +2.5% YoY increase in August.

To put this into perspective, home sales prices have increased in nearly every month since 2013, except for a brief period in 2023.

The largest YoY increase over this period was recorded in May 2021, at +24.3%.

The recent decline comes as the total number of homes for sale rose +0.9% MoM in October, to 1,526,984, the largest total since early 2020, as housing demand weakened.

US housing is cooling off.

The Nvidia situation is evolving.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has completely changed his view on Nvidia, $NVDA, over the last 7 days.

Last Sunday, Bessent called for a “dramatic shakeup” at Nvidia and said its board needed to hire a new CEO from “outside” the company.

Today, when asked about Jensen Huang returning as CEO, Bessent said:

“Well, Jensen is on the outside now.”

When pressed on whether Jensen Huang should return, Bessent said, “I think we have to see where the buck stops,” clearly leaving the door open.

This comes just 2 days after President Trump publicly said Jensen Huang should “apologize and return.”

Something is happening behind the scenes.

By comparison, during the 2008 Financial Crisis, gold's biggest 3-month drawdown was -22.2%.

Meanwhile, silver prices are down -38.7% since the start of September, putting them on track for their biggest 3-month rolling decline since 2008, when prices fell -45.3%.

By comparison, silver's largest 3-month rolling decline on record was -63.6% in 1980.

Gold and silver are experiencing historic selling pressure.

History says last week's volatility will soon be met by dip buyers.

The Volatility Index, $VIX, jumped +16.6 points this week, to 35.9 points, its highest weekly close since April 2025.

This marks its 5th-largest weekly increase on record.

Following the 4 weekly VIX spikes of at least 16.5 points since 1990, the S&P 500 rallied +5.1% on average over the next trading day.

The index also gained +3.3% over the following week, on average, with positive returns in all 4 historical occurrences.

Over the next 3 months, the S&P 500 returned +5.9% on average.

In the most recent occurrence, following the post-Liberation Day VIX spike in April 2025, the index rallied +22.7% over the next 3 months.

History suggests the market is set for a relief rally.

US technology ETFs are seeing massive wave of deleveraging:

The 3x leveraged long Semiconductor ETF, $SOXL, is down -90% from its June peak, to its lowest since September 2025.

This marks its 2nd-largest drawdown since the fund's inception in March 2010, surpassed only by the -91% decline during the 2022 bear market.

By comparison, the fund dropped -89% during the July 2024-April 2025 period.

Meanwhile, the 3x leveraged long Nasdaq 100 ETF, $TQQQ, is down -53% from its June peak to its lowest since early April.

Since October 5th alone, the fund has dropped -51%.

For perspective, $TQQQ fell -61% during the February-April 2025 drawdown.

Leveraged tech funds have experienced a historic liquidation wave.

There is a lot of discussion today about AI recruitment. Is it all bots?

Here is how OJ is currently recruiting:

After putting out a public notice to gather proposals for an analyst, we evaluated them but then also three of us personally drove to a local Ivy League business MBA program, sat down for meetings, and talked with graduates over coffee.

That was super high signal.

After that, we followed up, and they excited our other partners in a zoom interview, or didn’t. The right people can assert themselves across multiple mediums. We’re highly engaged for super-interested talent only.

My takeaways:
-Elite employers are of course recruiting face to face. People will travel for talent, as we did.
-Elite colleges matter. Speaking for ourselves, we go to the best.
-But I was a trailer park kid. I went to state schools. I was never Ivy.
-OJ seeks out extraordinary enthusiasm and talent, but doesn’t care where it comes from if excellence is demonstrated. If someone has an extraordinary story and wants to work for us, let us know.
http://Orangejuice.com 

We seek to find talent in all forms, while warning that the baseline is very high.

Morgan Stanley's Adam Jonas in new @SpaceX note:

"While we were at Starbase to watch Flight 15, we couldn't help but notice how much the city has transformed over even the last few months. In just a few years, Starbase has transformed from a small rocket testing site into arguably the most advanced spaceport in the world, a testament to SpaceX’s pace of execution in the world of atoms.

A few ongoing projects worth following:
• >1 GW Compute Campus
• Starpipe: an 8 mile nat gas pipeline currently planned to be operational by January that connects the LNG export terminal at the Port of Brownsville to Starbase to supply the liquid methane needed for high-cadence Starship launches.
• Gigabay: Starbase's Gigabay is a massive vertical assembly facility for Starship and Super Heavy Boosters with 24 work cells (vs. 6 at the two existing 'Megabays').

Investors who doubt SpaceX’s ability to execute large capital projects, such as Terafab, compute, solar, and telecommunications infrastructure, should at least follow the developments at Starbase, Texas. Even better, fly down for a launch."

What has happened in the past following the biggest weekly declines?

Stocks have tended to bounce back with above-average forward returns (1-Year: +26% vs. +11% in other periods).

Does that always happen? No. There are no certainties in markets, only probabilities.

Thank you to everyone who joined us in Miami for our inaugural Investing Through the Cycles (ITC) conference.

To the attendees who traveled from all around the world, it meant a lot to me that you made the trip. Some of my favorite moments were between sessions, when I finally got to meet people in person who have been part of the ITC community for years.

To our speakers, thank you for making the time to join us and for sharing how you think about markets. One of the reasons I wanted to put this conference together was to hear from people who can look at the same market and come to very different conclusions. I appreciated how willing you were to explain your thinking and challenge one another’s views.

A special thank you to Dana Howell @thedanahowell  for organizing the conference. Dana thought through so many of the little details that made people feel welcome. I saw how much care went into bringing the weekend together, and I’m grateful for all of it.

I’m glad we got to spend the weekend together, and I hope to see you again next year.

The frontier AI labs vacuumed up the world's knowledge and are now selling it back to us, while lobbying Washington for rules that choke off open-source competition, calling it safety.

You don't snuff out competition from a position of strength. If America doesn't want Chinese open source models, it should build its own, which is exactly what Jensen was pushing for. You can't out-China China by being China.

Then there's the fear. The heads of the leading labs signed a statement putting AI extinction risk alongside pandemics and nuclear war, then came to market anyway. If they believed it, they should never have been allowed to. They've pushed the most extreme job-loss forecasts too. AI is already impacting the job market, not sugar-coating it, but their fearmongering is out of all proportion. It's eroding the psyche of free societies, feeding unrest, and handing governments more control in the name of protection.

We've seen this playbook with climate doom: tell people the world is ending, invest in the "fix", lobby for the rules that protect their boondoggles. Even Bill Gates now says climate change won't end humanity, and nuclear, long shunned by the doomers, is back in favour.

This is the technology that could unlock longevity and energy abundance. Locking it behind a regulatory moat is the worst outcome for everyone outside it. 

Intelligence is becoming a commodity. The "effective altruists" at the frontier labs building it are trying to turn it into a feudal system.

Bitcoin is the asset built for the world that's coming. Pristine digital collateral: no counterparty, no issuer, no one who can print more of it. In a hyper-financialised economy where debt has outgrown liquidity since 2021, that matters more every year.

The liquidity cycle is approaching its turn. The 2027 refinancing wall leaves policymakers one realistic option, more liquidity, and Bitcoin has historically led when it comes. The next few months could be dicey. Buying into the teeth of the storm is uncomfortable, but it's usually where the best returns are made. The 3-4 years after look like the best setup I've seen in this asset class.

Around Bitcoin, crypto is growing up. New token supply across the Top 200 has fallen from about 25% a year in 2021 to about 4%, protocols now pay holders, and small teams run some of the most profitable businesses per employee ever built. It's what I have called crypto's Payback era.
